title: A sheaf on an affine inverse limit is a colimit
statement:
Let $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ be a directed inverse limit of affine schemes with
affine transition maps, and write $p_i:X\to X_i$. For every torsion abelian
sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$, the sheaves $p_{i,*}F$, with their
canonical transition maps, form a compatible system and the canonical
morphism

$$
\varinjlim_ip_i^{-1}p_{i,*}F\longrightarrow F
$$

is an isomorphism. (*Source:* Stacks Project,
[Tag
`0EYN`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYN).) In the Stacks Project this is a special case of Sites, Lemma 7.18.5,
[Tag `0EXJ`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EXJ), via
Lemma 59.51.2, [Tag
`0EYL`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYL) (the affine etale site of an affine limit is the colimit
of the affine etale sites of the stages). The first step of that reduction,
the descent of finitely presented algebras along the colimit of rings, is proved
in this chapter as [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent].
The affine and torsion case recorded here is the one used in this chapter.

proof.text: Use the fixed universe convention and small sites. The directed index set is nonempty, and its opposite is cofiltered. Every $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because it is affine. The projections $p_i$ are affine by the affine-transition limit theorem. Apply the affine-etale-site colimit theorem: after its coherent strictification the finite-cover affine etale sites $\mathcal C_i$ form a strict system, with colimit site $\mathcal C$ equivalent to $X_{affine,\Et}$. Write $u_{ji}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ and $u_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C$ for the base-change functors, so $u_j u_{ji}=u_i$; write $f_{ji}$ and $f_i$ for their site morphisms, and $a_{ji}:X_j\to X_i$ for the geometric transition morphisms. Object descent in that theorem gives $U=u_i(U_i)$ up to isomorphism for every $U$ of $\mathcal C$. Restriction from each small etale site to its affine site is an equivalence on abelian sheaves. Precomposition with a covering-preserving and covering-reflecting site equivalence is an equivalence on abelian sheaves: a quasi-inverse also preserves coverings, and the two functor isomorphisms give inverse restriction isomorphisms. Combine these equivalences with the strictification and colimit-site equivalences, and denote the resulting equivalences by $R_i:\Ab((X_i)_{\Et})\to\Ab(\mathcal C_i)$ and $R:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(\mathcal C)$.

source.place: Tag 0EYN (lemma-linus-hamann), reduction via Tag 0EYL (lemma-colimit-affine-sites), qcqs case, and Topologies Tag 04HR (lemma-alternative)

proof.text: Let $\mathcal F=RF$, and put $\mathcal F_i=f_{i*}\mathcal F=\mathcal F\circ u_i$. These identify with $R_i(p_{i*}F)$: at an affine etale $W\to X_i$, both evaluate to $F(W\times_{X_i}X)$, with restriction along $W'\to W$ induced by $W'\times_{X_i}X\to W\times_{X_i}X$. The fibre products are affine since $p_i$ is affine. For an abelian sheaf $A$ on $(X_j)_{\Et}$, both $R_i(a_{ji*}A)$ and $f_{ji*}R_jA$ evaluate at $W$ to $A(W\times_{X_i}X_j)$ with these restriction maps; the fibre products are affine since $a_{ji}$ is affine. These formulas are also natural in morphisms of sheaves, so they identify the right adjoint functors. For $G\in\Ab((X_i)_{\Et})$ and $H\in\Ab(\mathcal C)$, the equivalences and adjunction give natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(R p_i^{-1}G,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(p_i^{-1}G,R^{-1}H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,p_{i*}R^{-1}H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R_iG,f_{i*}H)$. Thus $R p_i^{-1}$ identifies with $f_i^{-1}R_i$. For the transitions, the corresponding chain is $\operatorname{Hom}(R_j a_{ji}^{-1}G,H_j)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(a_{ji}^{-1}G,R_j^{-1}H_j)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G,a_{ji*}R_j^{-1}H_j)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(R_iG,f_{ji*}H_j)$, giving $R_j a_{ji}^{-1}\cong f_{ji}^{-1}R_i$. The comparisons preserve units and counits because these are the adjoints of identity morphisms under the displayed Hom bijections.

source.place: Tag 0EYN, reduction to the affine sites; Topologies Tag 04HR; direct images evaluated on affine objects

proof.text: For $j\ge i$ the strict equation of functors gives $\mathcal F_i=f_{ji*}\mathcal F_j$. Define $\varphi_{ji}:f_{ji}^{-1}\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal F_j$ to be the counit $\varepsilon_{ji,\mathcal F_j}$, the adjoint of the identity $\mathcal F_i\to f_{ji*}\mathcal F_j$. Use the inverse-image composition comparisons determined by these adjunctions; step 2 identifies them with the canonical geometric comparisons. For $k\ge j\ge i$, the composite-adjunction counit formula gives $\varphi_{kj}\circ f_{kj}^{-1}\varphi_{ji}=\varepsilon_{kj,\mathcal F_k}\circ f_{kj}^{-1}(\varepsilon_{ji,f_{kj*}\mathcal F_k})=\varepsilon_{ki,\mathcal F_k}=\varphi_{ki}$. For the identity functor, the adjoint of the identity is the identity under its canonical adjunction comparison, so $\varphi_{ii}=1$. Set $G_i=f_i^{-1}\mathcal F_i$ and let $t_{ji}:G_i\to G_j$ be $f_j^{-1}\varphi_{ji}$ after $f_i^{-1}\cong f_j^{-1}f_{ji}^{-1}$. Functoriality and the displayed equality give $t_{kj}\circ t_{ji}=f_k^{-1}(\varphi_{kj}\circ f_{kj}^{-1}\varphi_{ji})=f_k^{-1}\varphi_{ki}=t_{ki}$ under the canonical comparisons, and $t_{ii}=1$. If $\varepsilon_i:G_i\to\mathcal F$ is the counit, the composite-adjunction counit formula for $f_i=f_{ji}\circ f_j$ reads $\varepsilon_j\circ t_{ji}=\varepsilon_{j,\mathcal F}\circ f_j^{-1}(\varepsilon_{ji,f_{j*}\mathcal F})=\varepsilon_{i,\mathcal F}$. These formulas use the comparisons defined by successive adjunction Hom bijections; their associativity follows from associativity of composing those bijections. Step 2 identifies the resulting transitions and counit cocone with the geometric ones.

The category of abelian sheaves on $X_{\Et}$ has all small colimits. The equivalence with abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$ therefore supplies the colimit $H=\varinjlim_iG_i$. More explicitly, transporting a colimit cocone through an equivalence preserves its universal property because the equivalence gives bijections on all Hom sets and every target is isomorphic to one in its image. The compatible counits of step 3 induce $e:H\to\mathcal F$ by the colimit universal property.

source.place: Tag 0EXJ, the canonical map from the sheaf colimit

proof.text: Fix an object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and choose $i,U_i$ with $u_i(U_i)=U$, using step 1 (an isomorphic representative gives the same conclusion). Apply the abelian-sheaf clause of the colimit-of-sites section formula to the system $(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{ji})$ constructed in step 3. Its hypotheses hold: the sites and functors are the strict finite-cover system from step 1, the site-system index is the small cofiltered category $I^{op}$, and the identity and cocycle laws were proved in step 3. For fixed $i$, the slice of arrows $j\to i$ in $I^{op}$ is the cofiltered poset of $j\ge i$; the section colimit is over its opposite, with arrows $j\to k$ for $k\ge j\ge i$. This is the nonempty filtered tail of the original directed poset. It identifies $H(U)$ with $\varinjlim_{j\ge i}\mathcal F_j(u_{ji}(U_i))$. In this formula the map from a stage is the adjunction unit for $f_j$, evaluated at $u_{ji}(U_i)$, followed by the colimit coprojection; the transition from $j$ to $k$ is the unit for $f_{kj}$ followed by $\varphi_{kj}$. Thus the formula includes the actual maps, not just an abstract isomorphism of groups.

source.place: Tag 09YN (lemma-colimit), abelian version as recorded by the cited node; application in Tag 0EXJ

proof.text: Every term of that section diagram is canonically $\mathcal F(u_j u_{ji}(U_i))=\mathcal F(U)$. Its transition $j\to k$ is the identity under these identifications: it is the unit $\mathcal F_j\to f_{kj*}f_{kj}^{-1}\mathcal F_j$ followed by $f_{kj*}\varphi_{kj}$, and $\mathcal F_j=f_{kj*}\mathcal F_k$, so the adjunction triangle identity applies to the counit $\varphi_{kj}$. Likewise, the composite of a stage map in step 5 with $e(U)$ is the unit $\mathcal F_j\to f_{j*}f_j^{-1}\mathcal F_j$ followed by $f_{j*}\varepsilon_j$, hence is the identity on $\mathcal F(U)$ by the same triangle identity. The tail $j\ge i$ is nonempty and directed: it contains $i$, and a common upper bound of $j,k$ is still in the tail. The identity cocone on this constant diagram is colimiting in abelian groups: for any cocone into a group $B$, its homomorphisms $h_j:\mathcal F(U)\to B$ satisfy $h_j=h_k$ by comparing both with $h_l$ at a common upper bound $l\ge j,k$; hence the unique factorization is $h_i$. Consequently the particular map $e(U)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0EXJ, final paragraph: the section diagram is constant with identity maps

proof.text: This holds for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$. The inverses $e(U)^{-1}$ commute with restriction, by multiplying the naturality equation for $e$ by these inverses, and therefore form an inverse sheaf morphism. Thus $e$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. Transport it back through the restriction equivalence of step 1. Step 2 identifies each $G_i$ with the restriction of $p_i^{-1}p_{i*}F$, step 3 identifies every transition and counit, and step 4 identifies their colimit by its universal property. Hence the transported map is exactly $\varinjlim_i p_i^{-1}p_{i*}F\to F$. This proves both the compatible-system assertion and the asserted canonical isomorphism for the given torsion abelian sheaf.
